title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (§49, 'Homomorphismes de M_{0,3}'). The setting appears to be the following; the identifications are interpretive. M_{0,3}^~ seems to be a profinite group of Teichmüller/GT type. It contains as a normal subgroup the profinite completion S^ = \hat{\mathfrak S}^{+}_{0,3} of the oriented cartographic group <ρ,σ | σ^2 = ρ^3 = 1>, i.e. \hat{PSL_2(Z)}. Its quotient Γ_{0,3}^~ contains Γ_Q = Gal(Q̄/Q).

The previous page sets up a closed subgroup G with S^ ⊂ G ⊂ M_{0,3}^~ and χ(u) ≡ 1 (mod 3). Each u in G then acts by u(ρ) = int(α_0)ρ and u(σ) = int(β_0)σ, with 'cocycles' α_0, β_0 : G → S^. These are the loop-equation data: a GT-like parametrization of an element by how it conjugates the order-2 and order-3 generators. G(0) and G[0] = Norm_G(L_0^S) are stabilizer subgroups attached to the cusp 0. Here L_0^S = closure of <ε_0> is the inertia (cusp) subgroup, with ε_0 = σρ.

This page. Grothendieck takes a continuous surjection φ: G → M onto a profinite group M, to be thought of as a finite quotient or 'level'. He pushes everything forward:
- 𝔾 := φ(S^), which is normal in M;
- M(0) := φ(G(0)), M[0] := φ(G[0]), L_0 := φ(U_0).

He records (10) M(0) ⊂ M[0] ⊂ Norm_M(L_0) and (11) L_0 ⊂ 𝔾 ∩ M[0]. The images of ρ, σ, ε_0, ε_1 in 𝔾 still satisfy (12): σ^2 = ρ^3 = 1, σρ = ε_0, ρσ = ε_1, and ε_1 = σ(ε_0) = ρ(ε_0).

In (13) the restricted cocycles α, β are formalized on SG = {(u,f) ∈ G × S^ | fu ∈ G[0]}. This is the inverse image of G in an extension SM_{0,3}, and the subgroup f = 1 is identified with G[0]. Composing with φ gives (14) α, β : G[0] ⇉ 𝔾. These satisfy (15): for x = φ(u_0) ∈ M[0], x(ρ) = int(α(u_0))ρ and x(σ) = int(β(u_0))σ inside 𝔾.

Purpose. The next page asks whether α and β depend only on x = φ(u_0) and not on the lift u_0. A priori they are determined only modulo the centralizers of ρ and σ in M. Using the cocycle rule, this is equivalent to α(J), β(J) ⊂ Ker φ, where J = Ker(G[0] → M[0]). The aim is to descend the loop-equation cocycles from the big profinite GT-type group to a quotient M, giving a 'finite-level' version of the loop equations. The margin note on p. 494 says Grothendieck later judged this whole section unnecessary in view of an interpretation via pro-sets.
errors: No mathematical error is visible on this page. (10) is right because G[0] normalizes U_0, so M[0] normalizes L_0. (11) is right because U_0 lies in both S^ and G[0]. The relations (12) check: σ(ε_0) = σσρσ^{-1} = ρσ = ε_1 and ρ(ε_0) = ρσρρ^{-1} = ρσ = ε_1.

Notation is inconsistent. In (13) α, β are first said to be restrictions to 'M_{ρ,σ}[0]', but they are actually defined on G[0] (or SG). In (15) the same letters α, β denote both the maps and their values. The well-definedness gap (dependence on the lift u_0) is not addressed here; it is treated only on the next page.

ideas.what: Pushing the GT-type loop-equation cocycles (α, β), defined by u(ρ) = int(α)ρ and u(σ) = int(β)σ, down along a surjection to a quotient profinite group M, with images of the inertia and normalizer subgroups
ideas.modern_name: finite-level / quotient approximation of Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type actions on \hat{PSL_2(Z)} (cartographic group); compare 'GT-shadows'
ideas.usually_credited_to: Profinite GT: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; finite-quotient approximations ('GT-shadows'): Dolgushev and collaborators (c. 2020s); dessins-related work by Lochak, Schneps, Nakamura and others
ideas.where_published: The general program (action of Gal(Q̄/Q) on cartographic groups) appears in Esquisse d'un programme; this specific construction appears only in these unpublished Longue Marche sequel notes

ideas.what: Presentation of the oriented cartographic group with σρ = ε_0 and ρσ = ε_1 as cusp loops, and ε_1 = σ(ε_0) = ρ(ε_0)
ideas.modern_name: PSL_2(Z) ≅ Z/2 * Z/3 and its parabolic elements

ideas.what: Auxiliary group SG = {(u,f) ∈ G × S^ | fu ∈ G[0]}, used to formalize the restricted cocycles

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a framework for when the loop-equation cocycles (α, β) of an element of a GT-type group descend to a finite quotient M of the cartographic or Teichmüller tower. The condition he derives on the next page is α(J), β(J) ⊂ Ker φ. This anticipates the recent idea of approximating \hat{GT} through compatible data on finite quotients ('GT-shadows', Dolgushev et al.). It is done here for the cartographic group \hat{PSL_2(Z)} with the cusp normalizer structure, which is not the setting usually used.
missed.quote: Considérons un groupe profini M, et un homom. (continu) surjectif φ : 𝒢 ⟶ M
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical precursor of finite-level GT approximations, here phrased via the (2,3,∞) orbifold group and the cusp normalizers. It is only modestly relevant, since Grothendieck himself marked the section as superseded.

missed.claim: The descent hypothesis — α and β depending only on φ(u_0) — is formulated, but the section is marked in the margin as useless because of a reinterpretation through pro-sets, so the thread was abandoned here.
missed.quote: Toute cette section ... est en fait inutile, à cause de l'interprétation sur des pro-ensembles
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Low impact; it mainly documents Grothendieck's own change of approach.

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine set-up: pushing GT-type cocycles to a quotient and recording images of subgroups. The idea of finite-level descent loosely foreshadows GT-shadows, but nothing on the page is a finished result, and the author abandoned the section.
transcription_corrections: Throughout, 𝒢 in the transcription is the group G from the previous page, a closed subgroup of M_{0,3}^~.
The margin note 'ss-groupe distingué de M' refers to 𝔾 = φ(Ŝ^+_{0,3}). It is correct, since the image of a normal subgroup under a surjection is normal.
In (15) the manuscript reads 'pour x ∈ M[0] de la forme φ(u_0)'. The handwritten 'M[a]' there should be read as M[0].
The page number in the bottom-left margin is 495.
